answer: Under dynamic opportunity-cost bonds, an adversary’s marginal payoff from identity multiplication follows a downward spiral bounded by collateral escalation, rendering replica profits strictly negative. A subgame-perfect slashing matrix enforces credible punishment, so any fable of costless Sybil capture collapses into dominated deviation. Equilibrium convergence is not a sable abstraction: strict Nash uniqueness holds because forged identities inherit identical penalties across all subgames.
